extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of art history and architecture; critics and scholars of medieval/Renaissance sculpture
extracted.subtask_description: Produce informed descriptive and evaluative prose about architectural sculpture (capitals, personifications, vices/virtues) with attention to iconography, craftsmanship, symbolism, historical typology, and comparative judgment against canonical exemplars (e.g., Giotto, Spenser).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sculptural skill / craftsmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the technical execution of carving (detail, modelling, finish).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: E.g., 'the paws laid, with great sculptural skill' — note crispness of forms, finish of drapery, anatomical fidelity; coarser work is judged later or inferior ('The sculpture ... very coarse and bad').

rubrics_metrics.name: Legibility of inscriptions and epigraphic clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether inscriptions remain readable and supply identification/meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated note that inscriptions are often 'illegible' or 'undecipherable' and that loss of inscriptions impedes identification; copies or Renaissance recensions may restore meanings. Condition (weathering, broken bars) affects decipherability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithfulness to canonical iconography
rubrics_metrics.description: How well a figure embodies the standard/expected attributes and posture of the virtue/vice (e.g., Fortitude with lion-skin and shield as a tower).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether key attributes are present: costume (lion's skin), instruments (sword, scales, compasses), postures (hand gestures), and whether the conception matches canonical examples (Giotto vs later copies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolic accuracy and appropriateness of attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: Correctness and aptness of the symbols chosen to signify a concept (e.g., anchor for Hope is inaccurate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vulgar or anachronistic symbols; prefer symbols that logically map to the virtue/vice (Giotto's bridle on Temperance's lips, sword she binds to scabbard). Note explicit criticisms: 'anchors are not for men... inaccurate.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual nuance / philosophical depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the depiction shows subtlety in the idea represented (e.g., Temperance as moderator of all passions rather than mere abstinence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for deeper allegorical content and distinctions (Greek vs medieval conceptions), not just superficial oppositions (Temperance vs Gluttony). Favor representations that express the full intellectual or theological concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power of expression / emotional intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: The capacity of the sculpture to convey emotion, suffering, vigor or moral quality (e.g., Avarice 'marvellous for power of expression').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate facial features, gestures, and bodily tension; high marks for intensity without caricature (see Avarice example: 'features hunger-bitten... without the slightest caricature').

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of caricature; restraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance between expressive exaggeration and dignified realism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise for expressive realism 'yet without the slightest caricature'; criticism when figures degenerate into mere grotesque or vulgar exaggeration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality vs hackneyed imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the depiction uses fresh, thoughtful symbolism or relies on 'vulgar' and frequently repeated clichés.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text criticizes 'vulgar and most frequent conception' and 'grievously hackneyed and vulgarized' images; award originality and condemn cliché (e.g., Spenser's more noble renderings are preferred to common pictorial conventions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative evaluation against canonical exemplars
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluating a work by comparison to established masters (Giotto, Pisan sculptors, Spenser's poetic personifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author repeatedly judges Venetian capitals as 'inferior' or 'not at all approach[ing]' Giotto; use canonical works as benchmark for nobility, symbolism, and execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iconographic completeness / inclusion of distinguishing traits
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of the essential distinguishing element(s) that define a virtue/vice (e.g., Prudence's forethought, Temperance's bridle and sword).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticises omissions: 'forethought ... is never enough considered or symbolized.' Grade higher when the sculptor includes the trait that most sharply defines the concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical/stylistic authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness of style to the period intended (mediaeval vs Renaissance differences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize period character: 'peculiar beauty of most of the Italian conceptions' vs Renaissance 'confused with angels'; prefer historically coherent types (Giotto's mediaeval focus vs Renaissance ornament).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of personification / conceptual precision
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the personified figure unambiguously communicates the intended moral/abstract quality (e.g., distinguishing avarice from covetousness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author notes moralists' confusions and emphasizes that correct conceptual labeling matters; precision in captioning and attributes reduces ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy and expressiveness of small details
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of small touches to convey meaning effectively (e.g., buckle shaped like a cloven heart, 'wearing' of a portesse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise subtle details that carry symbolic weight ('subtle touch of truth'); note how a few strokes can 'exalt the principal figure' and supply profound meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative or programmatic arrangement / composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Placement, sequence and prominence of figures in the architectural program (diagonal placement of the Creation of Man, conspicuous sides).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how composition and placement (which side is diagonal/is conspicuous) contribute to meaning and emphasis; capitals that reflect programmatic logic score higher.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of animal symbolism and mounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness and effectiveness of animals or mounts as symbolic devices (e.g., Gluttony on a swine, Envy on a wolf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether animal attributes reinforce the moral/characterological idea; note when animals become trite or misapplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of literary/allegorical tradition
rubrics_metrics.description: How well the sculptural representation engages or corresponds with literary personifications (Spenser, Dante, classical tradition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author compares sculptural figures with Spenser's and Dante's characters; higher value when sculpture harmonizes with respected literary allegory and philosophical intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: State of preservation and its effect on interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which weathering, breakage, or restoration alters reading of the sculpture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many capitals are 'defaced' or 'broken away' which 'embarrasses' identification; adjust evaluation acknowledging loss of information and reliance on copies for reconstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dignity of character / noble expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability of the work to convey dignity and noble character through features and bearing (e.g., 'thin, thoughtful and dignified' portrait-head).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe head attitudes, caps, and facial restraint; note efficacy of 'few touches' to express superiority or national character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of moral oppositions and program logic
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether virtues and vices are arranged and contrasted in a way that clarifies their relationships (e.g., placement of Miseria opposite Cheerfulness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate capitals as part of a moral program: do oppositions make sense and illuminate the intended ethical scheme? Ambiguity (uncertain labels like 'Miseria' vs 'Misericordia') reduces effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the human figure and physiognomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of figure types, facial modelling and physiognomic expression to convey personality and moral state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise for figures where 'signs of dignity of character' are appreciated; criticize crude or 'stupid' faces that undermine the concept (e.g., 'a knight, with a heavy and stupid face' for Pride).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of costume and accoutrement
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy and meaningfulness of clothing, helmets, crowns, or other dress elements in period and symbolic context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: 'crested helmet', 'noble cap' bound in a fillet, 'chain armor'—they should support identification and historicity rather than distract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iconographic program accuracy (astrological/learned motifs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correctness in scholarly or learned iconography (e.g., arrangement of planetary houses according to astrological tradition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Eighteenth Capital attempts to represent planetary houses; assess alignment with known astrological assignments (Sun = Leo, Moon = Cancer, etc.) and note missing/broken signs (Capricorn missing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative richness and didactic clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which the sculpture tells a compelling moral or didactic story accessible to viewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Figures that include subsidiary scenes (e.g., Justice with predella showing safe riders and dancing people) enhance narrative content; prefer clear didactic scenes over obscure or mutilated ones.
